title: Huygens
note: ESA's Huygens Titan probe as launched (1997): the entry assembly (front shield, back cover) closed around the descent module. Frame: z up = the probe's +Xp (from the front shield toward the orbiter), origin at the separation plane on the axis, where the fore dome meets the central ring; x = +Yp, y = +Zp (huygens_um Figs 2.2-13 to 2.2-15 axes). Built as its own model and placed on Cassini through the spec's includes.

sources.quote: Figs 2.2-5/2.2-6 (Xp along the axis), 2.2-13/2.2-15 (Z up, Y right seen from the top), 2.2-14 (Y to the left seen from below)
Fig 2.2-5: nose 375 and back cover 610 either side of the separation plane, 103.5 from the shield nose to the dome nose; Fig 2.2-6: 636 overall, 272 fore dome, (73), 261, (25)

stations.note: 272 + 73 + 261 + 25 = 631, so the experiment platform sits 5 mm above the dome's base; the ring's height (97) is estimated from Fig 2.2-6

shield.value: 60 degree half-angle sphere-cone, nose radius 1.25 m, shoulder radius 0.0486 m, 620.5 from the nose to the rim; shell 60 mm (estimated from the hatching)

sources.quote: Table 1 p.9: 'Nose radius 1.2501 m; Heat shield half cone angle 60°; Shoulder radius 0.0486 m'
'a 2.700 m diameter, 60-deg sphere-cone configuration with an open back face. The nose radius is 1.250 m'

shield_rear.value: rear face: Prosial (white) outside the back cover's footprint, the bare carbon structure inside it

sources.quote: 'The outer part of the rear face is coated with a 2 mm.-thick layer of thermal insulation (Prosial)... A back cover, inside which is the Descent Module itself, protects the central portion.'

back_cover.value: stepped cone: Ø1790 base, 151.5 up, 45 x 45 chamfer, then Ø1249.8, Ø686.6 at 17.8° and a Ø321.7 flat top at 10°, 610 above the separation plane; two access doors, a break-out patch for the PDD on the flat top, two antenna caps on the top cone, three SEPS recesses, a bump for the DISR cover

sources.quote: Fig 2.2-5 dimensions; p.14: 'Back cover is an aluminium stiffened shell protected by Prosial including the following items: two access doors, a break-out patch for the PDD located on the flat top of the shell... two shaped antennae caps on the top cone, 3 recesses for the SEPS accomodation, 1 bump located on the lower cone to accomodate the DISR cover'; Fig 2.2-9

back_cover.note: recess, door, cap and bump sizes estimated from Fig 2.2-9 (a perspective sketch)

descent_structure.value: aluminium fore dome and after cone joined at the central ring; three titanium vertical columns between the platforms; one access door in the after cone
